title: Investigate intermittent quota double-counting when project aliasing occurs during subaccount promotion
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We observe intermittent double-counting of token/embedding usage when a subaccount is promoted to a first-class project and the project alias mapping update happens concurrently with in-flight requests. Affected customers see a short spike in reported usage (2x) for the affected window; bills and quotas are impacted. This looks distinct from prior key-rotation races (notably not a leaked API key), and reproduces when project alias records are updated in the same commit that migrates subaccount IDs to the new project namespace.

Why this matters:
- Incorrect billing and quota enforcement for customers (potential overcharge or premature throttling).
- Breaks Dedicated reserved capacity assumptions when attribution is duplicated across old and new project IDs.
- High severity for mid-market/enterprise customers with strict quotas and billing audits.

Observed behavior / signals:
- Spike in metering rate for Project A at 12:43 UTC on 2026-02-28; two distinct project IDs (old-subaccount-123 and proj-7821) each show identical token counts.
- Ingress logs show single request ID routed through gateway with two downstream attributions applied within ~50ms.
- Rate limiter counters incremented on both project buckets, causing transient quota exhaustion for the new project.
- Dashboard: /dashboards/metering/duplicate-attribution shows 0.6% of requests in the week had >1 attribution.
- SQL snippet used to validate duplicates: SELECT request_id, array_agg(distinct project_id) as projects, sum(tokens) FROM metering.events WHERE time >= '2026-02-28T12:40:00Z' AND time <= '2026-02-28T12:50:00Z' GROUP BY request_id HAVING cardinality(array_agg(distinct project_id)) > 1;

Steps to reproduce (dev environment):
1) Create subaccount S under org O and simulate 50 concurrent streaming generation requests using the same API key bound to S.
2) Trigger subaccount promotion job that creates project P and writes alias mapping row (aliases.project_id -> canonical project_id) while streaming requests are still active.
3) Observe metering pipeline and rate limiter: certain requests get attributed to both S (old namespace) and P (new).
- Repro rate ~ 1-3% when promotion overlaps with high concurrency; increases with batching enabled.

Initial hypothesis:
- Race in attribution pipeline where first-stage attribution (gateway mapping) and later-stage reconciliation (project alias canonicalization) both emit attribution events without atomic deduplication when alias updates are in-flight.
- A downstream consumer (metering-aggregator) is subscribing to both pre-canonical and post-canonical topics during the migration window; dedupe key uses request_id+project_id (so different project_ids => duplicate tallies).

Files / links / artifacts:
- Investigation doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/ENG-660212
- Repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-harness/pull/142 (branch: eng-660212-repro)
- Chart: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/duplicate-attribution
- Query runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/billing-investigations

Mitigations attempted so far:
- Hotfix: temporarily paused the alias promotion job for ongoing large migrations (reverted promotion job at 2026-03-02 04:12 UTC) — reduced incidence to near-zero during paused periods.
- Added an aggregator-side filter to ignore events where project_id resolves to an alias already seen for the same request_id within 5s (heuristic) — reduced duplicate counts but not fully accepted due to edgecases and lack of upstream guarantees.

Root-cause candidate and proposed fix:
- Root-cause: non-atomic alias creation combined with asynchronous event emission from gateway and canonicalization service. Both services emit attribution events that are independently consumed by metering and rate-limiter subsystems. Lack of an idempotent canonicalization layer or global dedupe key that normalizes project references leads to double-counting.
- Proposed fix (three parts):
  1) Gateway: do not emit final attribution until alias canonicalization has completed for that request OR include both project_id and canonical_project_id in the emitted event (short-term safer payload).
  2) Metering & rate-limiter: switch dedupe key to canonical_project_id if present, falling back to project_id; add a short-lived in-memory request_id cache in aggregator to avoid counting the same request twice when canonicalization events arrive later.
  3) Migration: implement promotive migration steps with write-ahead alias propagation, where the alias record is written and fully materialized (ensured by synchronous commit) before marking the subaccount as promoted (makes promotion idempotent).

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy aggregator change to use canonical_project_id as primary dedupe key to 10% of ingestion nodes (billing-2026.03-canary). Monitor duplicates and latency impact for 48h.
- Phase 2: change gateway emission to include canonical_project_id when available (feature flagged).
- Phase 3: update promotion job to write-ahead alias and ensure synchronous propagation; coordinate with Console migration UI to gate large promotions behind scheduled windows.
- Phase 4: deprecate heuristic aggregator filters.

Acceptance criteria:
- Duplicate attribution rate < 0.01% in canary after 48h under matched load.
- No measurable increase (>1%) in ingestion latency at aggregator.
- Regression tests added to repro harness covering concurrent promotion + streaming workloads.
- Postmortem and customer notifications for impacted billing windows completed.

Next steps (owner: Miguel):
- 2026-03-03: finish aggregator patch and run canary on staging (PR #327).
- 2026-03-05: run large-scale repro in staging with production-like batching/streaming (engines: gptx-8b).
- 2026-03-10: extend rate-limiter unit tests for canonicalization-aware dedupe.
- 2026-03-13: prepare rollout checklist and customer communication draft (billing team).

Notes for postmortem and customer remediation:
- For affected billing windows we can reconcile using deduped request_ids (where available) and issue invoice credits if overcharged. We need a safe SQL reconciliation path that groups by canonical_project_id computed by joining alias mapping snapshots at event time.
- Add an alert to PagerDuty if duplicate_rate > 0.1% for 15m rolling window.
